newsitem.title: UK: Chaos of French trucker strike spreads to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Chaos of French trucker strike spreads to Britain.

text.p: British police said on Wednesday they were controlling the movement of freight vehicles into southeastern ports because the French truckers' strike had spread traffic chaos across the Channel.
All freight vehicles travelling to the ports of Dover and Ramsgate were being stopped and diverted to a nearby holding area until a place became available on a ferry, said police.
They estimated there was a queue of up to 800 lorries waiting to cross the Channel.

"The situation has now deteriorated and there is a minimum of 12 hours delay for freight leaving the port of Dover," said police inspector Ian Smith. Last week's fire in the Channel Tunnel has also had an impact as only limited freight traffic is currently being allowed through it.
French truckers' leaders and employers were locked in new marathon talks on Wednesday as truckers kept up their road blockades that were starting to throttle the economy.

Wednesday was also to test wider union disaffection in France. The Communist-led CGT union was urging workers to rally at the truckers' barricades to show support and step up pressure on Prime Minister Alain Juppe to drop austerity policies.

Truckers and haulage bosses, meeting in an annex of the Transport Ministry in Paris as the strikes entered a 10th day, were debating strikers' demands for higher pay, shorter hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.

The strikers have set up nearly 200 truck blockades on major routes and blocked refineries and fuel depots around France, closing some petrol stations, forcing factory closures and squeezing supplies of goods like fruit and fish.
